part.text:
Done. Since React 19.1/Next 16.4 canary here lack `<ViewTransition>` support, I wired the native View Transitions API into the App Router:

**Shared element morph (grid ↔ detail)**
- `app/view-transition.ts` — `startNavigationTransition()` wraps `router.push` in `document.startViewTransition`, holding the new-state capture until the route commits (signaled by `NavigationEvents` on pathname change, with a 600ms `skipTransition` failsafe).
- `app/ProductCard.tsx` — on click, clears `view-transition-name` from all thumbnails, names only the clicked one (pre-capture), and records the slug in sessionStorage.
- `app/product/[slug]/page.tsx:48` — hero carries the matching `view-transition-name` in SSR HTML (verified in raw output).
- `app/ProductImage.tsx` — on back-nav, the grid re-names the last-viewed thumbnail via sessionStorage so the hero morphs back into place.

**Directional slides** — `TransitionLink` sets `data-nav-direction` on `<html>`; CSS slides old/new root left for forward, right for back (`globals.css:159`).

**Suspense → content** — loaded content gets `.animate-in` (fade + rise) when the skeleton swaps out; the detail page streams dynamically so this genuinely triggers.

**Reduced motion** — JS skips `startViewTransition` entirely, and CSS confines pulse/entrance/slide animations to `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` with a `reduce` kill-switch on all VT pseudos.

One known limitation: the browser's native back button can't be intercepted by the App Router, so only in-app navigation animates. Build and typecheck pass.
